newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOKYO NAPHTHA SLIPS ON CRUDES, CONTANGO UNCHANGED.
newsitem.headline: TOKYO NAPHTHA SLIPS ON CRUDES, CONTANGO UNCHANGED.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha weakened on Friday, tracking a sharp overnight loss in crude prices, while Abu Dhabi informed Japanese naphtha lifters of its initial offer price for the term-year starting in September, traders said.
Open-spec naphtha for second-half October was quoted at $206.00/$208.00 per tonne, down from late Thursday's $210.00/211.00.

First-half October was assessed about $1.00 to $1.50 below the second-half October level. It was traded at $207.75 between a South Korean trader and a Japanese trading house on Thursday, market sources said.
The one-month spread from second-half September was discussed at minus $3.50/minus $2.50, little changed from Thursday's levels.

Abu Dhabi National Oil Co (ADNOC) offered its term naphtha at around $22.00 per tonne over the ADNOC formula for one-year term supply contracts beginning in September, compared with a $7.15 premium for the current term year ending this month.

Potential buyers -- one oil firm negotiating on behalf of a group petrochemical firm, and a trading arm of a western oil major -- are each expected to import about 100,000 tonnes of ADNOC cargoes in the new term year, traders said.
